reason: The text is a historical narrative (2 Kings 24-25) describing the fall of Jerusalem, the siege by Nebuchadnezzar, and the exile of Judah. It records events involving both elite figures (kings, officials) and common people without making any philosophical claim about inherent superiority of the elite. In fact, the narrative shows the king Zedekiah (elite) committing evil acts and suffering severe consequences (capture, blindness, death of his sons), while common people also suffered greatly through siege and exile. The passage does not assert or imply that any class is inherently better than another—it is descriptive of political and military events, not prescriptive about human worth or capability.
